paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

", "output": "Okay, voice memo for the Montreal trip planning before I forget the details. We are looking at July eighteenth through the twenty-second, and that is four nights unless Mom decides she wants to come a day later. She has not confirmed yet, so I should not count her in the room total for now. Ben, Maya, and I are definitely going, and Grandma Ruth is a maybe. I want to keep the plan flexible without making it sound like we already booked everything. Maya has camp until the afternoon of the seventeenth, and Ben can only take Monday through Friday off, so the train dates are a little awkward. We could leave Friday morning and come back Tuesday, or leave Saturday and have one less full day. I think Friday is better if the fares are reasonable.

For the train, we need to get from Albany-Rensselaer to Montreal on the Adirondack, and I wrote down that it leaves at 10:12 in the morning and gets in around 7:30 in the evening if it is on time. I need to check the current schedule before we buy anything because that time may be from last summer. Our seats should be together and preferably near a window, but I do not need to pay extra for a table if that makes the tickets much more expensive. The station in Montreal is central, and we can take a taxi to the hotel if the bags are too much for the metro. We will have one medium suitcase, one small roller, and Maya's backpack. Mom says she can manage her own tote, but I should ask her how heavy it is.

For the hotel, the Old Port is convenient, but prices are high, and the metro is not far from the Plateau either. I saved two places. One is the Maple House on Saint Paul Street, which has family rooms and breakfast, but the reviews mention street noise. The other is an apartment near Sherbrooke station with a washer and a small kitchen and no breakfast. I should compare the total price after taxes and check whether the apartment has an elevator because Mom's knee gets sore on stairs. The room needs either two beds or a bed and a pullout sofa. We can share one bathroom, but it has to be private, and we should ask about storing luggage before check-in. I have not sent an inquiry yet.

For the things I need to settle first:
1. Check the train timetable and the change policy for all four possible travelers before choosing a departure.
2. Compare the hotel totals and ask whether a room for three can be changed to four if Ruth joins us.
3. Ask Mom if she can travel on Friday and whether she wants to stay all four nights.
4. Talk to Maya about packing and tell her she cannot bring her big stuffed fox if she wants to carry her own backpack. She has brought it up twice and said, “Fox has to see the Old Port.” I can let her take the smaller fox or pack the big one in the suitcase if there is room.

For getting around, I want to use the metro most days, but the first evening we may be tired and should probably take a cab to the hotel. We can buy an Opus card for each adult and check whether Maya needs her own card or can ride free at her age. I think she is still under the child fare cutoff, but I need to verify it. The Biodome is not in the Old Port, so we should group it with the botanical garden if we go there instead of making two trips across town. The Science Centre is easier to reach on foot and might be a better rainy-day choice. The weather is uncertain in July, so leave one afternoon open rather than filling every hour.

Maya wants to see the Old Port Ferris wheel and the little shops, and Ben wants to visit the archaeology museum. I would like to walk up Mount Royal if the weather is clear, but I do not want to promise the whole family a long hike. Mom can wait at the lookout cafe, or we can take the bus part of the way. She said, “I will decide when I see the hill,” so keep that as an option, not a scheduled activity. We should book the museum only after checking opening hours and whether children need a timed ticket. The Ferris wheel can be decided that day if the line is not too long, and if it is windy, we can skip it without making a fuss.

Food needs a little planning because Maya will eat eggs, cheese, plain pasta, and most fruit, but refuses spicy food. Ben is happy to try anything, and Mom does not eat shellfish. We can have breakfast at the hotel if the price difference is small; otherwise, get yogurt and fruit from a grocery store nearby. I want to find one casual place for poutine, but check for a non-spicy option, and somewhere with soup or salads for Mom. No one needs a fancy dinner reservation every night. Maybe book one dinner for Saturday and keep the rest open. We should carry water bottles and a few snacks for the train and not rely on the cafe car in case it is closed or crowded.

For the budget, I set aside about twelve hundred dollars for lodging and around six hundred for the train, but those are estimates, not limits yet. I have not checked whether the train fare includes the bags we plan to bring, and I do not know if the apartment charges a cleaning fee. Add local transport, museum tickets, meals, and maybe one taxi to the list before deciding what is affordable. I also need to check our travel insurance and make sure Mom has her medication in the original containers and enough for an extra day in case the return train is delayed. She can bring her own small pill organizer too, but the prescription labels should stay with the bottles.

Last thing: I should make a shared note with the confirmation numbers after we actually book and give Mom a printed copy because she prefers paper. Maya can help choose two activities, but she should know that the plan might change if it rains or if somebody is tired. I do not want to cram every idea into four days. The main goals are to spend time together, see a few things we all enjoy, and get back without turning the whole trip into a schedule. We leave Saturday morning, the eleventh of July, and drive home Wednesday the fifteenth. We are staying in a small rental in Saugatuck, not Holland, and the address is on the confirmation email. I saved it in my phone and printed a copy for the glove box. The owner said the key code will arrive by text on Friday afternoon, and the earliest check-in is four o’clock, so we should not plan lunch around getting into the house early.

Mara is driving from Madison, and we are coming from Evanston. Our plan is to meet at the public beach lot near the playground at one thirty on Saturday, if the drive goes normally. I put the address in the group chat, and Mara replied, “That is the lot with the blue picnic shelter, right?” I said yes and told her to call if she cannot see the lake from the entrance. We should keep the first stop simple: sandwiches from the grocery store and a walk on the beach, not a big restaurant meal, because the kids get carsick when we go straight from the car to a crowded table. We can bring the folding blanket from the hall closet.

1. Before we leave the house

I am putting the reservation printout in the glove box and checking that the car insurance card is current. The rental has one parking space, so Mara needs to leave her car at the public lot overnight on Saturday, and we can take her bags over in our car. There is a second free space behind the rental, but it belongs to the neighbor, and the owner specifically said not to use it. I checked that our cooler fits behind the passenger seat and that the stroller folds before we load everything. The small blue suitcase is for both kids and their swim things. The gray bag is for clothes and toiletries, and the red tote is food for the drive.

For the food, I wrote down apples, crackers, cheese sandwiches, and two water bottles each. I need to add the little container of ginger candies that helps with the car sickness. The crackers should stay up front where we can reach them without unloading the trunk. The rental has a full kitchen but no coffee maker, so Mara is bringing her small French press, and we will buy coffee after we arrive. I have asked the owner whether there is a kettle, and she has not answered yet, so we should not assume there is one. I will bring the kids’ reusable cups and their usual cereal because changing breakfast on the first day tends to cause arguments.

On Sunday, we want to visit the nature center in the morning and leave the afternoon open for swimming if it is warm. The center opens at ten, and the trail map says the shortest loop is just under a mile. Mara can take the older child on that loop while I stay near the entrance with Leo if he is tired. We do not need to reserve anything for the walk, but the center requests a small parking donation in cash. I have twelve dollars in the coin pouch and should put a few singles in there too. If the weather turns, we may spend more time at the library on—but I have not checked its Sunday hours yet.

Monday is the day we have reserved the two-hour kayak lesson for three adults and one child at nine thirty. The younger child is not old enough for the lesson and will stay with me on shore. That is what the instructor confirmed by email on Tuesday. The meeting point is the launch beside the marina, not the public beach, and we should arrive twenty minutes early to fit the life jackets. The confirmation says closed-toe water shoes and a change of clothes. I told Mara, “Please do not bring the big cooler to the launch,” because there is no place to leave it there. We will carry towels and a dry shirt in one backpack.

Tuesday is flexible, and I would rather choose one outing after we see how everyone is doing than book another activity now. The old lighthouse is about thirty minutes away, and the farmers market downtown is listed for Tuesday morning, but I need to confirm that it is open this week. There is a small grocery store two blocks from the rental and a larger one near the highway. If we need medicine, the pharmacy closes at six according to the sign I saw online, so if anyone needs a prescription filled, we should call before we drive over. I will bring the thermometer and the children’s allergy medicine from home.

Before we head back Wednesday, we have to strip the beds, put used towels in the basket, and take the kitchen rubbish to the bins by the garage. The owner asks guests to leave by ten, but our drive is short enough that we can pack the car after breakfast and still leave on time. I will check the fridge for anything we have left, and Mara can count the beach toys so they do not end up under the seats.
